questions.question: What is the PC 200 salary indexation on 1 January 2026?

mitosis.answer:
The PC 200 indexation on 1 January 2026 is 2.21%. It applies to actual salaries, sector minimum scales and the guaranteed average minimum monthly income [be_fr_pc200_index_2026][int_index_calendar_2026][slk_2025_12_22_final][tkt_2026_0019_mertens].

Where sources disagree:
- 2.13% (Pro-Pay October forecast) vs 2.21% (final): 2.21% wins. The forecast was provisional and depended on the Nov/Dec health index [be_propay_forecast_pc200]. The same applies to the ~2.2% internal outlook [int_outlook_2025_11] and the Team Kortrijk note of 18 Dec [int_nl_nota_index_2025_12], which predates the final figure.
- Delta's payslips showed 2.13% because of a manual override that the 24 Dec update did not overwrite. Remove the override and pay the 0.08 pp difference retroactively [tkt_2026_0012_delta].

Scope differences:
- Brouwerij Van Dessel: its company CAO applies 2.21% on 1 February 2026, on base salary only. The 145 EUR brouwerijpremie is excluded and gets +2% on 1 July. January is unindexed, except that the indexed sector minimum applies where base salary would fall below it [cao_vandessel_2019][tkt_2026_0015_vandessel].
- Other committees: PC 124 is 0.21859% (quarterly) and PC 330 is 2% [tkt_2026_0021_maes][tkt_2026_0024_az]. The Slack claim of 2.21% "across the board" is wrong; official sources win [slk_2026_01_06_pc124].

questions.question: What indexation should Brouwerij Van Dessel apply in January and February 2026, and on which salary components?

mitosis.answer:
Direct answer: Brouwerij Van Dessel applies no indexation in January 2026 and 2.21% on 1 February 2026, on gross monthly base salary only [cao_vandessel_2019, art. 2–3; eml_vandessel_budget].

January: pay without the new index. The one exception is an employee whose base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum. That employee gets the sector minimum from 1 January [cao_vandessel_2019, art. 5].

February: the brouwerijpremie (€145) is excluded from the index. It stays at €145 and rises by a fixed 2% on 1 July [cao_vandessel_2019, art. 4].

Where sources disagree:
- Rate: 2.13% (Pro-Pay forecast, October) vs 2.21% (final, confirmed by Agoria, Acerta, Securex). 2.21% wins because it is the final published figure [slk_2025_12_22_final; tkt_2025_0870_vandessel].
- Timing and base: the sector rule says 1 January on all effective salaries and minimum scales. The Van Dessel CAO says 1 February on base salary only. The CAO wins for Van Dessel only. Other PC 200 clients keep the sector rule.

Correction needed: Van Dessel's January payslips wrongly applied 2.21% on total pay, because the CAO flag was lost in the engine migration. The correction is planned in the February run [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel; slk_2026_01_09_vandessel].

Note: the separate Delta issue (2.13% manual override, difference paid retroactively) does not apply to Van Dessel.

questions.question: Bouwgroep Maes has construction workers and office staff. What indexation applied to each in January 2026?

mitosis.answer:
Bouwgroep Maes got two different indexations in January 2026, one per population.

Construction workers (PC 124, 58 people): the quarterly indexation of 0.21859% on 1 January 2026, applied to hourly wages and to the food and housing allowance [tkt_2026_0021_maes][eml_maes_recovery].

Office staff (PC 200, 9 people): the annual indexation of 2.21% [tkt_2026_0021_maes][eml_maes_recovery][cfg_maes].

Where sources disagree:
- Slack claimed 2.21% "across the board" for all Maes employees, on the health index [slk_2026_01_06_pc124].
- The ticket, the recovery email, the client config sheet and the official PC 124 sources say 0.21859% for PC 124, and 2.21% for PC 200 only [tkt_2026_0021_maes][eml_maes_recovery][cfg_maes].
- The official sources win. They are authoritative and consistent with each other. The Slack message is informal, and 2.21% is the PC 200 figure wrongly applied to PC 124. The config sheet also says never to apply one population's indexation to the other [cfg_maes].

questions.question: Give Verhaeghe Logistics an overview of 2026 indexation and minimum wages per entity. Should their Dutch expats get 27% under the 30% ruling?

mitosis.answer:
**Short answer:** No, Verhaeghe's Dutch expats should not get 27% in 2026. The maximum is 30% through 2026 and drops to 27% from 1 Jan 2027 [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe][eml_verhaeghe_nl_30pct]. Employees who already received the allowance in December 2023 keep 30% under the transitional rule. That covers two of the three planners. The third moves to 27% from 2027.

**2026 indexation per entity**
- Belgium, PC 140.03 (drivers): 2.18% on 1 Jan [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe][be_sdworx_press_food_horeca_transport].
- Belgium, PC 200 (office): 2.21% on 1 Jan, annual [tkt_2026_0230_verhaeghe][be_bbtk_indexeringen_jan2026].
- Luxembourg: +2.5% on 1 June 2026, index 992.24 [eml_verhaeghe_lu_frontaliers]. The unqualified minimum is 16.0192/h [lu_ssm_2026].
- Netherlands: there is no automatic indexation. The minimum wage (21+) was 14.71/h for Jan–Jun 2026 and is 14.99/h from 1 July [nl_minimumloon_jul2026].

**Where sources differ**
- **NL minimum wage:** 14.71 applies to Jan–Jun, and 14.99 wins from 1 July because it is the newer official rate. Six warehouse staff at 14.75 must be raised to 14.99 [tkt_2026_0260_verhaeghe_nl]. As of today that is overdue, so check for back pay.
- **Other committees:** The indexation rate differs by joint committee, so do not apply one rate across them. PC 124, PC 302 and PC 111/209 do not concern Verhaeghe. For reference, the final PC 302 figure is 2.189%, which wins over the 2.1% November estimate [be_pc302_index_2026].

January is paid without indexation, except where the indexed sector minimum applies [cao_vandessel_2019] [tkt_2026_0015_vandessel]. This changes the date and base, not the percentage. The CAO overrides the sector rule for that client only.
- Softwarehuis Delta: its payslips used 2,13% through a manual override. Remove it and pay the 0,08 pp difference retroactively [tkt_2026_0012_delta].

Ownership: sources disagree on the PC 200 contact. A Slack message of 5 Jan 2026 names Koen Janssens [slk_2026_01_05_owner]. The wiki update names Jan Peeters since 1 Sept 2025 [onb_ownership_2025_update]. The wiki wins because it is official policy and was never reversed.

questions.question: What is the PC 200 salary indexation on 1 January 2026?

mitosis.answer:
PC 200 salaries are indexed by 2.21% on 1 January 2026. This is the final figure [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026].

Scope: The 2.21% applies to effectively paid salaries, sectoral minimum scales and the guaranteed minimum monthly income [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026][be_acerta_pc200_index_2026]. I found no per-scope differences.

Calculation: Acerta uses the smoothed health index, (133,07 + 133,33) / (130,22 + 130,42) = +2.21% [be_acerta_pc200_index_2026]. No modified indexation mechanism applies, because the regulatory framework was not ready in time, so the normal rules apply [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026].

- Pro-Pay's October 2025 forecast: 2.13% [be_propay_forecast_pc200].
- Final figure: 2.21%, from Agoria, Acerta, Securex, SD Worx and Orbiss [be_agoria_pc200_index_2026][be_acerta_pc200_index_2026][be_securex_pc200_index_2026][be_sdworx_press_pc200_221][be_orbiss_pc200_221].
- Winner: 2.21%. The forecast was explicitly provisional, because the November and December 2025 health index figures were not yet known. The official figure replaces it [be_fr_pc200_index_2026].

Caution: SD Worx notes that 2.21% is specific to PC 200 and must not be copied to other joint committees [be_sdworx_press_pc200_221].
